practiceQuestions.q: On which date did the British Parliament pass the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indian Independence Act was introduced in the British Parliament on July 4, 1947, and received Royal Assent on July 18, 1947.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the British Prime Minister when the Indian Independence Act, 1947 was passed?
practiceQuestions.sol: Clement Attlee of the Labour Party was the Prime Minister of the UK during the transfer of power to India.

practiceQuestions.q: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 provided for the creation of which two independent dominions?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act partitioned British India into two independent dominions: India and Pakistan, effective from August 15, 1947.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, who was to be the head of the state for the new dominions until a new constitution was framed?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act provided that the British Monarch would remain the head of state for the dominions until they adopted their own constitutions.

practiceQuestions.q: Which office was abolished by the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act abolished the office of the Viceroy and replaced it with a Governor-General for each dominion.

practiceQuestions.q: What happened to the 'Paramountcy' of the British Crown over the Indian Princely States under the 1947 Act?
opts: It was transferred to the Indian Government
It was transferred to the Pakistan Government
It was retained by the British Crown
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act declared that the suzerainty of the British Crown over the Indian states lapsed, and with it, all treaties and obligations.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was appointed as the first Governor-General of the Dominion of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lord Mountbatten was appointed as the first Governor-General of the new Dominion of India.

practiceQuestions.q: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 empowered the Constituent Assemblies of the two dominions to:
opts: Remain part of the British Empire
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act gave the Constituent Assemblies full power to frame and adopt any constitution for their respective nations.

practiceQuestions.q: Which body was responsible for the demarcation of boundaries between India and Pakistan?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Radcliffe Commission was set up to demarcate the boundaries between the two new dominions.

practiceQuestions.q: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was based on which plan?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act was the legislative implementation of the Mountbatten Plan, also known as the June 3rd Plan.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the 1947 Act change the status of the Secretary of State for India?
opts: He became an advisor to the PM
practiceQuestions.sol: The office of the Secretary of State for India was abolished, and his functions were transferred to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the legal status of the laws passed by the British Parliament for India after August 15, 1947?
opts: They ceased to apply to India
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act stipulated that no Act of the British Parliament passed after August 15, 1947, would extend to either of the new dominions unless extended by a law of the legislature of that dominion.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the 1947 Act considered a 'transfer of power' rather than a 'grant of independence'?
opts: Because it was a British legislative act
Because the King remained the head
Because the army was controlled by UK
practiceQuestions.sol: It was a legal instrument passed by the British Parliament to transfer authority from the British Crown to the new Indian governments.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Act affect the Civil Services of India?
opts: Existing officers were allowed to continue
They were replaced by British officers
They were transferred to the UK
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act ensured that the existing civil servants appointed by the Secretary of State would continue to serve the new dominions with the same rights and privileges.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the role of the Governor-General under the 1947 Act?
opts: Constitutional head acting on advice of ministers
Commander of the armed forces only
practiceQuestions.sol: The Governor-General became a constitutional head, acting on the advice of the dominion's cabinet.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was a key feature of the 1947 Act regarding the Princely States?
opts: They were forced to join India
They were given the option to join either India or Pakistan or remain independent
They were automatically part of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act allowed Princely States to decide their own future, leading to the complex integration process.

practiceQuestions.q: The 1947 Act provided that until the new constitution was framed, the governance of the dominions would be carried out in accordance with:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act provided that the Government of India Act, 1935 would continue to be the governing framework until the new constitution was adopted.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the 'Royal Assent' on July 18, 1947?
opts: It marked the end of British rule in India
It was the date of partition
practiceQuestions.sol: Royal Assent made the Indian Independence Act a law, setting the stage for the formal transfer of power on August 15, 1947.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the 1947 Act treat the 'Title of Emperor of India'?
opts: It was retained by the King
It was dropped from the royal titles
It was transferred to the President of India
It was changed to 'Emperor of Commonwealth'
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act provided for the omission of the title 'Emperor of India' from the royal titles of the British monarch.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was NOT a power given to the Constituent Assemblies by the 1947 Act?
opts: To declare war on any country
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assemblies were given legislative powers to frame constitutions and enact laws, but they were not given the power to declare war as a sovereign state until full independence was realized.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. It provided for the partition of India and the creation of two independent dominions.
2. It gave the Princely States the freedom to join either India or Pakistan or remain independent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Act formally partitioned India and gave the Princely States the choice of accession.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Independence Act, 1947 abolished the office of the Viceroy.
2. The Governor-General was to be appointed by the British Monarch on the advice of the dominion cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Viceroy office was replaced by the Governor-General, who was appointed by the King on the advice of the dominion government.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was passed by the British Parliament in July 1947.
2. It came into force on August 15, 1947.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Act was passed on July 18, 1947, and the transfer of power took place on August 15, 1947.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constituent Assemblies:
1. The Act empowered the Constituent Assemblies to frame their own constitutions.
2. The Act prohibited the Constituent Assemblies from repealing any existing British laws.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Act explicitly gave the Constituent Assemblies the power to repeal or amend any Act of the British Parliament, including the Independence Act itself.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Independence Act, 1947 provided for the partition of Bengal and Punjab.
2. The boundary commission was headed by Lord Mountbatten.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Boundary Commission was headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, not Lord Mountbatten.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 1947 Act ended the British control over the Indian Army.
2. The Act provided for the division of the Indian Army between India and Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Act facilitated the division of assets, including the armed forces, between the two new dominions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was the last major act passed by the British Parliament regarding India.
2. It granted full sovereignty to the two dominions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is technically incorrect because the dominions were initially 'Dominions' under the British Crown, not fully sovereign republics until they adopted their own constitutions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Act allowed the Governor-General to make modifications to the Act for the purpose of bringing it into operation.
2. This power was to be exercised until March 31, 1948.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the power was to be exercised until March 31, 1948, but the Act itself was the source of this power. Actually, the date was March 31, 1948, so both are correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Act provided that the British Monarch would no longer have the right to veto laws passed by the dominion legislatures.
2. The Governor-General was empowered to give assent to any law on behalf of the King.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Act removed the King's veto power and empowered the Governor-General to act on his behalf.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was the result of the failure of the Cabinet Mission Plan.
2. The Act was drafted by the British government in consultation with Indian leaders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Act was primarily drafted by the British government based on the Mountbatten Plan, and while Indian leaders agreed to the plan, they did not draft the Act itself.
